statement: The start menu has no list of modes: its only rows are one or two players, each player's device, the computer's level, five comfort boxes and Start, so six of the eight Alpha modes have no menu entry.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a mode row on the existing menu plus the host's routing in render/core/main.gd; the Rail menus were one polish-day job, cost not recorded)
risk: Each mode's row is useless until that mode exists; build the row list from data so rows appear as modes land.

statement: The co-op horde mode does not exist: there is no horde design page, the henchmen page says it is paper only, and the sim's many-body match holds at most five bodies with no waves and no respawn.
cost_basis: comparable: the first co-op match was costed at about 14M tokens (docs/ep/proposals/co-op-2v2.md:86) and Research sized a three-body co-op slice at 10 to 12 slices (docs/research/co-op-brawler.md:165)
risk: The pair assumption runs through the sim (docs/research/co-op-brawler.md:171); a horde that regresses versus shows first as a golden mismatch in CI's parity job.
orb_question: Is a first horde of one or two players against waves of at most three weak bodies at a time (the sim's present five-body limit) enough for Alpha, with bigger waves after? Recommended: yes.

statement: Couch 2v2 cannot be started: the game's own host only ever starts a two-body match, the input hub has two player slots, and the only code that asks the sim for two fights is the LAN program.
cost_basis: comparable: drawing the partner's fight was costed at about 4.5M tokens (docs/ep/proposals/co-op-2v2.md:37); the sim side (two fights, hits across) is already built
risk: Two fights on one screen means up to four panes; frame rate and the per-screen flash register are the early warnings.
orb_question: For Alpha, is couch 2v2 two humans as a team against two computer fighters on a two-way split (the line-up the LAN 2v2 already uses)? Recommended: yes; four pads after Alpha.

statement: LAN play is not part of the game a tester would get: it is started by Windows shortcut files on a private program made by patching a scratch copy with the host PC's address baked in, and the desktop export presets leave the network code out.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a host and join screen with an address entry, the two calling lines on main, a Linux launcher, and Legal's review of the rule that keeps net/ out of desktop builds)
risk: Legal's rule (named RL-204 in net/lan.gd:4) excludes net/ from public desktop builds; the Alpha build needs a written exception or LAN stays a separate download.
orb_question: Do outside testers get LAN play in the Alpha build itself, or does LAN stay a private two-PC folder for you and the second player? Recommended: in the build, behind a Host and Join row.

statement: A LAN match cannot be rematched or left to a menu: the program plays one match and tells both players to close both windows.
risk: X-08's five full matches would need five restarts on both PCs today.

statement: There is no fighter select: a match's fighters default to the first two of the roster file, so player one is always the Protagonist and player two always the rival.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the sim already takes a setup key naming the fighters, sim/core/sim.gd:202 and sim/core/roster.gd:53-59)
risk: A mirror pick (two of the same fighter) needs a second palette to tell them apart; not evidenced as built.

statement: Custom planet setup does not exist: the menu has no planet row, and the planet generator takes a seed only, with no input for size, city count, climate or water.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (four generator inputs, their limits, a picker screen and the loading path that already exists, render/core/main.gd:452-454)
risk: Planet size changes the number of columns the whole sim assumes; a seed-only picker is the fallback if the four dials slip.
orb_question: If the four dials (size, cities, climate, water) cannot all land for Alpha, is a seed picker with a few named presets acceptable as the first custom planet? Recommended: yes.

statement: On main the rules that end a match the way the last played build did (knockout only by a finishing move, wear for an idle player, the last event after the time cap) are switched off, and on only in the two kept builds.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a data flip in a golden window; the checks ending_check and ending_team_check exist but are not in CI, per 01-inventory/I-02-sim-director.md:38)
risk: A build made from main's data ends matches by different rules from the one Orb judged.

statement: No mode smoke suite exists: the one smoke check drives the browser build by clicking fixed screen points and failed once when the menu layout changed, and the desktop workflow only plays a computer-against-computer bench on Linux with no run on record.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a scripted pad through menu, match, result, rematch and leave for each mode on the Windows and Linux desktop builds)
risk: Without it X-05 is checked by hand eight modes by two platforms on every candidate.

statement: LAN 2v2 exists only as two humans, one on each PC, against two computer fighters, and each screen shows only its own fight; the owner reported never seeing all four fighters together.
cost_basis: comparable: drawing the partner's fight, about 4.5M tokens (docs/ep/proposals/co-op-2v2.md:37)
risk: Drawing both fights puts two fights' effects on one screen; the proposal ties it to one flash register per screen (docs/ep/proposals/co-op-2v2.md:37).

statement: Every LAN match is the same match: the seed, the planet and the fighters are constants in the LAN code, so nothing a player picks reaches a LAN game.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the host's picks sent to the joiner before the match key is made)
risk: X-11's same-planet-on-both-LAN-PCs check is only ever exercised on one planet today.

statement: X-11's planet hash comparison is not a check yet: the planet fingerprint tool prints hashes with no verdict and is left out of the world checks, and every CI job runs on Linux only.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a stored expected line per seed and a run of the tool on the Windows build)
risk: A float difference between Windows and Linux in planet generation would show only as a LAN mismatch between a PC and a Deck.

statement: With a pad alone a player can go back to the menu but cannot close the game: the pause and match-over lists have no quit row, and the only quit is the keyboard's Escape, which closes the game at once with no question.
risk: A Deck tester leaves through the console's own button; a keyboard tester loses a match to a stray Escape.

statement: There is no practice mode: the grey reference dummy is third in the roster file but nothing in the menu or host can put it in a match.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a Practice row that starts a solo match against the dummy with a computer level that stands still; whether such a level exists is not evidenced)
orb_question: Should Practice against the dummy be a ninth Alpha mode, as the cheapest way to teach a newcomer? Recommended: yes as nice-to-have, built only after the mode row and fighter select.

statement: The time cap is a rules event at 11 minutes (14 in 2v2) with a pause, but no picture of the planet giving way was found in the drawing code, and the cap sits above the 6 to 8 minute match X-13 describes.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a ruling on the cap's time for Alpha; the picture is separate work)
risk: A tester whose match reaches the cap sees a freeze and a forced finish with no visible reason.

statement: The campaign is sim groundwork only (about 1,180 lines across three files) with its switch off, no caller in the game outside one validity check, and no screen; the recommendation is none for Alpha.
orb_question: Ship Alpha with no campaign, and write that down as the X-12 decision? Recommended: yes; the horde mode reuses the campaign's horde-stage design instead.

statement: The Rail menu the owner picked is switched off on main and on only in the played build, so the menu a main-built candidate shows is the older card.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a flag flip plus the screen sweep)

statement: Solo against the computer starts from the menu with a pad alone, and the menu's level row lists the three levels in the computer's data file and passes the choice into the match.
Two players on one PC start from the menu: the host claims a device for each player, and a second player who chose a pad that is not there is started against the computer instead of standing still.
A finished local match opens a match-over card with Play again, Menu and Send feedback (and Save where on), and Play again restarts with the same choices and no intro.

The sim already takes a match's fighters, a second fight and a planet seed as setup keys, and a 2v2 with hits across ends only when a team has nobody standing, so most missing modes are menu and host work rather than new rules.

The LAN folder of the played build ran its nine self-test rows (1v1, 2v2 apart and 2v2 together, at home-network and slow-link timings) with no script errors and every state check matched, and the LAN check runs in CI.
